body.statement: Under Assumptions \(\ref{ass:iid-sampling}\), \(\ref{ass:holder-regressions}\), \(\ref{ass:design-density}\), \(\ref{ass:characteristic-kernels}\), and \(\ref{ass:residual-kernel-lipschitz}\), there is \(K<\infty\) such that, with probability at least \(1-\alpha\), all \(d2^{d-1}\) risks and all \(d(d-1)2^{d-2}\) score-relevant residual-HSIC values lie in their cross-fitted bands, with \(w_R\le K\{\sqrt{\log(M_d/\alpha)/n}+a_n^2\}\) and \(w_H\le K\{\sqrt{\log(M_d/\alpha)/n}+a_n\}\). Boundedness of the kernels controls the held-out empirical fluctuation in \(w_H\), while Assumption \(\ref{ass:residual-kernel-lipschitz}\) is used only to convert the cross-fitted residual error into the additive \(a_n\) term. On this event, if \((G_0,f,p_N,P)\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{pair}}(d)\), every queried HSIC value belongs to \(\{0\}\cup[\lambda,\infty)\), \(2w_S<\delta_{\mathrm{pair}}\), and \(2w_H<\lambda\), then \(\widehat{\mathcal G}_n=\{G_0\}\). Without the two separation inequalities, interval propagation retains every compatible decision and reports more than one graph whenever the data do not separate zero from the positive-HSIC region.
body.justification: The finite-sample theorem ties singleton recovery to the primitive gain slack and an explicit pruning resolution while preserving abstention near the discontinuity at independence.
body.gap: Pfister et al. (2018, Theorem E.2 and Proposition E.3) and Shekhar et al. (2023, Theorems 6 and 7) do not jointly cover learned normalized risks, simultaneous residual perturbations, adaptive insertions, and separated-model graph confidence sets.
body.consumer: Users receive a certified labelled DAG only when both navigation and pruning margins dominate propagated uncertainty.
